lines: -description: Create a database migration to add a table, add columns to an existing table, add a setting, or otherwise change the schema of Ghost's MySQL database. Use this skill whenever the task involves modifying Ghost's database schema — including adding, removing, or renaming columns or tables, adding new settings, creating indexes, updating data, or any change that requires a migration file in ghost. Also use when the user references schema.js, knex-migrator, the migrations directory, or asks to "add a field" or "add a column" to any Ghost model/table. Even if the user frames it as a feature or Linear issue, if the implementation requires a schema change, this skill applies.

+description: Create a database migration to add a table, add columns to an existing table, add a setting, or otherwise change the schema of Ghost's MySQL database. Use this skill whenever the task involves modifying Ghost's database schema — including adding, removing, or renaming columns or tables, adding new settings, creating indexes, updating data, or any change that requires a migration file in ghost. Also use when the user references schema.ts, knex-migrator, the migrations directory, or asks to "add a field" or "add a column" to any Ghost model/table. Even if the user frames it as a feature or Linear issue, if the implementation requires a schema change, this skill applies.

1. Create a new, empty migration file: `pnpm gx generate migration <kebab-case-slug>` from the repository root. IMPORTANT: do not create the migration file manually; always use this script to create the initial empty migration file. The slug must be kebab-case (e.g. `add-column-to-posts`).

2. The above command will create a new directory in `ghost/core/server/data/migrations/versions` if needed, create the empty TypeScript migration file with the appropriate name, and bump the core and admin package versions to RC if this is the first migration after a release.

3. Update the migration file with the changes you want to make in the database, following the existing patterns in the codebase. Where appropriate, prefer to use the utility functions in `ghost/core/server/data/migrations/utils/*`. Write new migrations in TypeScript; existing JavaScript migrations are frozen and stay as they are.
-4. Update the schema definition file in `ghost/core/server/data/schema/schema.js`, and make sure it aligns with the latest changes from the migration.
+4. Update the schema definition file in `ghost/core/server/data/schema/schema.ts`, and make sure it aligns with the latest changes from the migration.
5. Test the migration manually from the repository root: `pnpm knex-migrator migrate --v {version directory} --force`
6. Roll the migration back to test `down()`: `pnpm knex-migrator rollback --v {previous version} --force`, then migrate forward again.

7. Run the migration integration test, which covers initialization, rollback, forward migration, and idempotency: `cd ghost && pnpm test:single test/integration/migrations/migration.test.js`. It needs MySQL running, which `pnpm dev` starts.
